claims.text: Controlled post-annealing aging can induce nucleation and uniform growth of nanoscale precipitates in a homogenized, predominantly single-phase refractory high-entropy alloy.
The aging-induced nanoscale precipitates will improve the strength–plasticity combination relative to the untreated homogenized alloy.
A narrow aging temperature-time window below the melting point is conducive to precipitate nucleation.
A suitable alloy composition can permit formation of a secondary nanoscale phase without precipitate coarsening.
The aging treatment will produce a uniformly distributed population of nanoscale precipitates within the matrix.
The nanoscale precipitates will obstruct dislocation motion.
The precipitate-containing microstructure will allow localized precipitate shearing or modified slip to operate as alternative plastic-deformation mechanisms.
The combination of dislocation obstruction and alternative plastic-deformation mechanisms will simultaneously increase yield strength and ductility.
The aged alloy will have higher yield strength than the untreated homogenized alloy.
The aged alloy will have greater ductility than the untreated homogenized alloy.
Improvement requires optimal control of precipitate size, distribution, and volume fraction.
Inappropriate aging temperature or duration, or an alloy composition unfavorable to precipitation, may eliminate the proposed benefits.
